label: prop:neutron-proton-mass-splitting
title: Neutron--proton mass splitting from quark crossing change
html:
Assume (\mathrm{H}_\alpha): a change of the quark-ordering traced volume \Phi is converted to energy by the nuclear binding scale \alpha = m_e \times 8G, as \alpha\,\lvert\Delta\Phi\rvert. Under (\mathrm{H}_\alpha), the model neutron--proton mass difference is

  \Delta m
  := \alpha \cdot
    \bigl\lvert
      \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) -
      \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d})
    \bigr\rvert
  \approx 1.054 \;\mathrm{MeV}

where \alpha = m_e \times 8G is the binding scale and \Phi is the quantum dilogarithm volume.

The volumes are the traced-volume closed forms evaluated at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) = 0.6126880371 at q_0, pairing each strand with every later strand. This gives \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) \approx -0.614886, \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) \approx -0.896395 and \lvert\Delta\Phi\rvert \approx 0.281509, so with \alpha = 3.7445 the model value is \Delta m \approx 1.0541 MeV.

Comparison with measurement. The CODATA splitting is m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx 1.29333 MeV, so the model value is about 18.5\% below it. This comparison is the empirical claim of the block.

A second model value. The corpus has a second, independent route to the splitting. The T^3 weight split of the z = q^3/(q^2+1) trace on the \gamma\gamma nucleon gives Q_\beta = \lvert t_{\mathfrak n} - t_{\mathfrak p}\rvert \cdot E_0 \approx 0.3254 MeV, where E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)) (tower-summed) is the corpus's derived hadronic scale. The decay kinematics m_{\mathfrak n} - m_{\mathfrak p} = Q_\beta + m_e then give \Delta m \approx 0.8364 MeV, about 35.3\% below the measured value. That route uses E_0 in place of (\mathrm{H}_\alpha). It fixes the size, not the sign: on its own it does not make the neutron the heavier nucleon. The two values come from different constructions, and neither is selected by its residual.

That is a claim about this construction, and not an exclusion: nothing here shows a quark-ordering volume cannot carry the splitting.

Two-term charge-insertion probe (record, not a derivation). The following facts about the 3-strand weight spaces W_p = (2,1) and W_n = (1,2) are proved: the quark-charge operators Q_iQ_j break the intertwiner P(q) between the two nucleon weight spaces; \mathrm{tr}(e_{(2,1)} V^3) = 2 - 3h^4 - h^6 on the Borromean word V^3 = (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3; and the closed forms of the adjacent-pair traces. These are statements about a charge insertion. Two features of how they were turned into masses are choices, not derivations:

  • The braid content comes only from omitting a pair. Summed over all three quark pairs, the charge insertion differs between W_n and W_p by -\tfrac13\,\mathrm{tr}(w) for every word w; that is static charge counting, with no braid dependence. The word-dependent "connected" term keeps the pairs 1–2 and 2–3 and drops 1–3. The Borromean word does not single out the adjacent pairs, since each of its three pairs crosses twice.
  • The scale is chosen. The figures were formed with m_e, with E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)) (a definition), or with \alpha_{\mathrm{bind}}, under four weightings (plain, K_n/K_p, K_p^3, q), and compared against the \mu–p tension, the Q_\beta residual and lattice benchmarks.

So the keV, ppm and ppb values recorded with these files describe selected combinations, are not predictions, and are not scored. The splitting still requires a quantity the framework does not yet derive.

Canonical quantum-trace weighting. On the three-strand tensor cube, the quantum trace \mathrm{Tr}(K^{\otimes 3}\,\cdot\,)/[2]_q^3 reproduces the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) and fixes the canonical weighting without free choice; the plain, K_n/K_p, K_p^3, and q weightings serve only as labelled comparisons. For the covariant insertion Q_{12}+Q_{23}+Q_{13} summed over all three pairs, the connected part vanishes on V^3, so the resulting two-term contribution to m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} is zero. Figures such as M_{\mathfrak{p}}^{\mathrm{QED,conn}} \approx +0.2201 keV, \Delta m^{\mathrm{QED,conn}} \approx -0.3317 keV, and a \mu–p tension of 8.06 ppb (0.37\sigma) arise only from the 1/3-normalised plain weighting restricted to adjacent pairs; they do not hold for the covariant quantum-trace form and do not resolve the \mu–p tension.
